summary.headline: All seven rows reviewed, no sampling. Two rows are supported outright and five are challenged, none of them on the boundary: every seam in this cluster holds from both sides and no cut is proposed. The two high-severity findings are both false statements about the Masoretic layer in measurement rows. At MT 42:16 the row clears a ketiv/qere as not a numeral when the read form there is the plural hundred-word, the multiplier the perimeter figure depends on, against a written form that is the cubit-word; the three parallel verses and the summary figure carry the hundred-word plainly. At MT 43:15 the row asserts a ketiv/qere and counts two variant verses in its span, but the corpus record of variant sites has no entry at that verse; what stands there is two editorial notes, one of them undisclosed, and the row then argues from the site that does not exist. The medium finding is an undisclosed editorial note at MT 43:11 in a three-verse row whose whole warrant is the Masoretic texture of those verses. The two low findings are a hundred-cubit figure attributed to the wrong pair of verses, and a south-side label on a chamber block whose own first verse reads the direction as east.

COVERAGE. All seven cluster rows located in the rows file by their own identifier field and reviewed; the cluster record independently lists the same seven row ids and the same span, MT 41:12-MT 43:27. One item per row, seven items, no sampling.

HEBREW COLLATION, ROWS. Every Hebrew run in all seven rows was extracted programmatically and tested as an exact substring of the witness: 47 runs, 47 present, 0 absent, and each one present at the verse the row cites for it. Five of the 47 are unpointed consonantal runs, the written forms of variant sites, and the running witness text does itself carry all five.

HEBREW COLLATION, MY OWN PACKET. Every Hebrew run in the finished deliverable was re-run back against the witness by exact path after the final write: 11 runs checked, 11 present, 0 absent. Every one of them was copied out of the witness by word index at build time, with a containment assertion that would have thrown rather than write an unverified string; none was retyped, re-pointed or assembled.

PUNCTA HAND-CHECK (the permanent MT 41:20 / MT 46:22 obligation). Hand-counted from the witness bytes: MT 41:20 carries exactly five U+05C4 upper dots and they all stand on the single ninth word of the verse; MT 46:22 carries seven; no other verse in the book carries U+05C4, and U+05C5 occurs nowhere in the book. The row asserting five, on one word, and two puncta sites in the book is exact on all three counts. The row makes this an affirmative disclosure, not a denial tucked behind a comma, so no rewording is owed on that ground.

PARAGRAPH MARKS, BOTH DIRECTIONS. Checked every claimed mark and every mark present. The corpus records no mark at all between the open section at MT 39:29 and the closed section at MT 43:9, so the claims of no mark in MT chs 40-42, none in MT ch 42, and none in MT 43:13-43:17 are all true; MT 39:29 is an open section and MT 43:9 a closed one, as claimed; the unmarked stretch is 103 verses, which the chapter counts 49 + 26 + 20 + 8 confirm; MT 43:27 carries two consecutive closed-section marks and is the one doubled mark in the book, 184 occurrences on 183 verses, counted as occurrences and never added to the verse total; no mark falls between MT 43:9 and MT 43:27. No row claimed a mark that is not there and no mark present in any row span is undisclosed.

PASEQ, ALL SEVEN ROWS, EXACT. Counts and verse identities checked against the corpus record: five occurrences over four verses at MT 41:12, 41:16 twice, 41:17, 41:19; three over two at MT 42:10 and 42:13 twice; two at MT 42:15 and 42:20; one at MT 43:8; one at MT 43:12; none in MT 43:13-43:17; none in MT 43:18-43:27. Every one matches. Intra-verse positions are not placeable from the extract and none was claimed or checked.

KETIV/QERE, ALL SITES IN THE CLUSTER. The corpus records eight variant verses in MT chs 41-43, of which seven fall in these row spans: MT 41:15, 42:9 with two notes, 42:14, 42:16, 43:11 with two notes, 43:16 and 43:26. Six of the seven are disclosed and characterised truly. The exception is MT 42:16, where the read form is the plural hundred-word and the row calls the variant not a numeral; the parallel verses MT 42:17, 42:18, 42:19 and the summary MT 42:20 all carry the hundred-word without a variant, which is what makes the site a numeral site. Separately, no variant verse exists at MT 43:15 in the corpus record, yet one row asserts one there and counts two variant verses in its span where there is one.

EDITORIAL NOTES, BOTH DIRECTIONS. The corpus records non-variant notes at exactly three verses in MT chs 41-43: MT 41:20, MT 43:11 and MT 43:15, of 71 such verses in the book. The note at MT 41:20 is disclosed and its content stated correctly. The note at MT 43:11 is undisclosed. MT 43:15 carries two notes and one of them is undisclosed, while the row recasts the other as a variant note.

DEVICE COUNTS, RE-DERIVED FROM BYTES. Four counts that the device inventory does not carry were re-swept over the witness with a consonantal-skeleton match and all four are exact as the rows state them: the glory idiom in 9 verses including MT 43:4 and MT 43:5; the river name in 8 verses including MT 43:3; the falling-on-the-face clause in 5 verses including MT 43:3; the conjoined divine-address form in 23 verses, a list that correctly does not include MT 43:10, whose form lacks the conjunction, which is exactly how the row handles it. Four further counts were checked against the inventory and match: the divine address at 93 verses with MT 43:7, MT 43:10 and MT 43:18 in it, the messenger formula at 122 with MT 43:18 in it, and the utterance signature at 81 with MT 43:19 and MT 43:27 in it.

CONTENT SPOT-CHECKS FROM BYTES. Verified at their verses: the two transport verbs in one verse at MT 42:1; the completion notice paired with a transport verb at MT 42:15 and the inner-house object it names; the measuring reed and first measurement at MT 40:5, so the circuit the row closes does open there; the clause-initial measure verb at MT 42:16 and MT 42:17 but not at MT 42:18 or MT 42:19; the direction word at the head of MT 42:10 and the south attribution at MT 42:12 and MT 42:13; the say-verb at MT 41:4 against the speak-verb at MT 41:22; the doubled title framing MT 43:12 at both ends; the twelve-by-twelve hearth figures at MT 43:16 and the fourteen-by-fourteen ledge at MT 43:17; the young bull at MT 43:19, the blood on four horns and four corners at MT 43:20, the second-day goat at MT 43:22, the seven days at MT 43:25 and 43:26; the return verb with no continuation particle at MT 44:1; the double doors at MT 41:23-41:24 and the door decoration at MT 41:25.

OUT-OF-SPAN REFERENCE FLAG ANSWERED. The cluster record places that flag on six of the seven rows. I read the flag detail and checked each referenced verse: every out-of-span reference in this cluster serves either the both-sides weighing the rulings require, or a book-level disclosure such as the other puncta site and the nearest paragraph marks, or the rejected-alternative argument, and each is true on the bytes. None is a defect and I recorded the answer in the evidence of each flagged item. The breadth of two of the lists, whole adjacent units of eleven and thirteen verses, is a structural question rather than an original-language one.

CITATION-SWEEP WARNING CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY. The suite report also carries a warning that one in-field quotation bound to MT 42:16 lacks a ketiv/qere disclosure beside it. That is a second, differently derived route to the same verse my high-severity finding rests on, and the fix I propose covers it.

Census over the corpus rows for the orchestrator: seven of the eight runs stand at 8 rows exactly as the brief states; the eighth, about a strict word-event onset, measures 7 rows.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: ROUTED OPEN QUESTION, INSTANCES COLLECTED AND NOT ADJUDICATED. Every written-form quotation in this cluster is rendered with the source's morpheme separator stripped: the corpus variant record carries those separators and the rows do not. The five sites are the galleries form at MT 41:15, the paired chamber and entrance forms at MT 42:9, the cubit-word at MT 42:16, the form-word at MT 43:11 and the altar-hearth word at MT 43:16. Each stripped rendering is nevertheless an exact substring of the running witness text at its own verse, because the running text itself prints the written form unpointed and unseparated. I found no read-form quotation anywhere in this cluster, so I have no apparatus-only read-form instance to add.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: This is the data the pending ruling needs, and in this cluster it points one way the routed question may not have anticipated: here the stripped rendering agrees with the running text and it is the variant record that carries the separators, so a normalizer keyed to the variant record would flag forms that the running text does contain.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: The untyped note at MT 43:15 says the edition has abandoned or added a ketiv/qere there relative to the printed critical edition. The corpus record of variant sites has no entry at that verse, which fits the abandoned branch, but the note text is disjunctive and I cannot settle which branch applies from the extract alone.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: It does not change the finding, which is that no ketiv/qere stands at MT 43:15 and the row asserts one. It does bear on how the corrected disclosure should be worded, and the answer is in the source XML rather than in the extract.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: The do-not-reuse census I measured over the corpus rows returns 8 rows for seven of the eight named runs, matching what my brief states, but 7 rows and not 8 for the run about a strict word-event onset.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: Reported because the gate threshold is counted in rows: that one run has one more row of headroom than the brief records. My own prose uses none of the eight runs nor any five- or six-word run inside them, checked programmatically over 36 derived runs.
